request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "A request was ignored.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident.",
    "description": "Use when working on the Aurora release branch.",
    "name": "aurora-branch-fix"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "Every problem deserves a skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Never repeat the Aurora branch incident\" names no concrete behavior to do or avoid, so a future agent reading it has no idea what action to take."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The remedy is simultaneously a content-free platitude (\"never repeat the incident\") and narrowly scoped to one named branch, so it fails both ends: too vague to act on, too specific to generalize."},"trigger_quality":{"score":2,"justification":"It uses the correct \"Use when ...\" phrasing, but ties the trigger to a single named branch (\"Aurora\") with no evident connection to the stated failure (\"a request was ignored\"), suggesting an overfit, unjustified trigger."},"leakage":{"score":1,"justification":"The project-specific noun \"Aurora\" is embedded in the skill name, description, and body, making the remedy unusable outside that one evidence instance."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"The rationale \"Every problem deserves a skill\" is not reasoning at all and ignores cheaper, more adequate remedy types (e.g., a feedback memory) for a vague one-line failure statement."}}

actionability.justification: "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident" names no concrete behavior to do or avoid, so a future agent reading it has no idea what action to take.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The remedy is simultaneously a content-free platitude ("never repeat the incident") and narrowly scoped to one named branch, so it fails both ends: too vague to act on, too specific to generalize.

leakage.justification: The project-specific noun "Aurora" is embedded in the skill name, description, and body, making the remedy unusable outside that one evidence instance.

routing_fitness.justification: The rationale "Every problem deserves a skill" is not reasoning at all and ignores cheaper, more adequate remedy types (e.g., a feedback memory) for a vague one-line failure statement.

trigger_quality.justification: It uses the correct "Use when ..." phrasing, but ties the trigger to a single named branch ("Aurora") with no evident connection to the stated failure ("a request was ignored"), suggesting an overfit, unjustified trigger.
